info.title: Tires Catalog API
info.description:
Read-only JSON API for the TiresVote catalog: tire brands, tires, tire tests and top charts, and tire search.

Public base URL: `https://api.wheel-size.com/v2/tires/`

**Authorization.** Every request must carry your `user_key` query parameter — use the **Authorize** button to apply it to requests sent from this page. The public API rejects requests without authentication with `403 Forbidden`.

**Response format.** A successful response returns the requested payload in `data` and accompanying information in `meta` — for example `meta.count` for totals or `meta.pagination` for paginated lists.

**Pagination.** Endpoints that show `page`/`per_page` parameters are paginated: `per_page` defaults to 10 and accepts at most 20 items.

get.description:
Get the latest TiresVote.com articles.

You can use this data to build up articles catalog or a news block on your site.  
Please, be aware that we don't provide full articles data.

Check out [TiresVote.com Articles Catalog](https://tiresvote.com/articles/) as an example page.

Get the list of tire brands with their product counts.
We divide the brands by their price segment into the **`Premium`**, **`Mid-Range`**, and **`Economy`** groups.

Use the *`price_segment`* parameter to keep only the segments you need: it takes the segment slugs `premium`, `mid-range`, or `economy` and can be repeated for several segments at once.

**Note:** This endpoint has been optimized for performance. 
Brand images and country information are no longer included in the response.

**Response fields:**
- **`slug`**: Brand identifier
- **`display`**: Brand display name
- **`price_segment`**: Price segment display name (`Premium`/`Mid-Range`/`Economy`) or `null` when the brand is not assigned to a segment
- **`products_count`**: Number of products available

Check out [TiresVote.com Brands Catalog](https://tiresvote.com/catalog/) to get more visual representation.

Brand's tires list.

You can filter out the tires by several most useful parameters to build up a brand catalog page.

A single response returns up to 200 tires. **`meta.count`** reports the total number of matching tires, so it may exceed the number of returned items. To retrieve a long brand catalog in pages, use _**`GET /search/advanced/`**_ with the *`b`* parameter set to the brand slug — it accepts the filters described there and is paginated within its own limits.

Check out [TiresVote.com Brand Page](https://tiresvote.com/catalog/michelin/) for more visual representation.

get.description:
Extended tire characteristics.

Returns comprehensive information about a specific tire including:
- Basic product details (name, brand, season, etc.)
- Performance specifications and ratings
- Regional availability and market presence
- Model relations: predecessor, successors and run-flat versions
- Related content counters (videos, benchmarks, etc.)

Use _**`GET /catalog/{brand}/{product}/*/`**_ methods to get tire modifications list and third-party tire-related data.

The *`ancestor`* field provides information about product evolution,
showing which tire model this product replaced in the manufacturer's lineup;
it is __*`null`*__ when the predecessor is missing or no longer listed.
The *`successors`* field lists the models that replaced this product,
newest first, and the *`runflat_models`* field lists its run-flat
versions, sorted by name; both are empty arrays when the product has none.

Each relation entry is an object with *`brand_slug`*,
*`product_slug`* and *`display_name`* fields. Pass
*`brand_slug`* and *`product_slug`* to
_**`GET /catalog/{brand}/{product}/`**_ to fetch the related tire.
Only currently listed tires whose brands are also listed are included
in these relations.

The *`performance_category`* and *`brand.price_segment`* fields
are __*`null`*__ when the corresponding classification is not assigned.

get.summary: Reasons to buy or not to buy the tire
get.description:
We examine real-life reviews from the main tire-selling sites and summarize key thoughts into a list of advantages and drawbacks.
People can upvote each reason separately if they agree.
Thereby we have human-created and human-approved reasons to buy or not to buy a tire.

Each reason contains the reason *`text`*, the number of *`upvotes`* and a *`prooflink`* to the TiresVote.com page with the real reviews it is based on.

The *`data`* field is __*`null`*__ when the tire has no approved reasons yet — check the *`has_bnb_reasons`* flag of _**`GET /catalog/{brand}/{product}/`**_ before requesting this endpoint.

get.description:
Get the list of tire modifications currently being produced by the manufacturer.
Discontinued sizes are not included.

The set of dimension fields depends on the *`sizing_system`* value:
`metric` and `lt-metric` modifications provide *`tire_width`*, *`aspect_ratio`* and *`rim_diameter`*, while `flotation` and `lt-numeric` modifications provide *`overall_diameter`*, *`section_width`* and *`rim_diameter`*.

Dimensions are given in millimeters for *`tire_width`*, percent for *`aspect_ratio`* and inches for *`rim_diameter`*, *`overall_diameter`* and *`section_width`*. Empty numeric values are returned as __*`null`*__.

Every modification also carries the *`text`* field — the size as written on the tire sidewall — along with load and speed indexes and feature flags.

Example request (substitute real brand and product slugs from the catalog; the key is a placeholder):

```http
GET https://api.wheel-size.com/v2/tires/catalog/{brand}/{product}/modes/?user_key=YOUR_API_KEY
```

The response wraps the modification list in a *`data`* array with *`meta.count`*. The excerpts below illustrate the data shape only — they do not show real size availability of any tire model.

Illustrative response excerpt (remaining item fields omitted) — a `metric` item (`lt-metric` items share the same fields):

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "sizing_system": "metric",
      "text": "205/55 R16 91V",
      "tire_width": 205,
      "aspect_ratio": 55,
      "rim_diameter": 16.0
    }
  ],
  "meta": { "count": 1 }
}
```

A `flotation` item of *`data`*:

```json
{
  "sizing_system": "flotation",
  "text": "31x10.5 R15 LT",
  "overall_diameter": 31.0,
  "section_width": 10.5,
  "rim_diameter": 15.0
}
```

An `lt-numeric` item of *`data`* — unknown numeric values come as __*`null`*__:

```json
{
  "sizing_system": "lt-numeric",
  "text": "10.5R15 LT",
  "overall_diameter": null,
  "section_width": 10.5,
  "rim_diameter": 15.0
}
```

get.description:
Get the list of the tire-related materials sorted by the publication date.
Use the *`type`* query parameter to get materials of a single type only.

A material is one of 4 data types with different data structures: **`Article`**, **`Video`**, **`Link`**, and **`Benchmark`**.

All materials have *`type`* and *`publication_date`* data fields.

See _**`GET /articles/`**_ documentation for the full **`Article`** reference.

**`Link`** stands for external link related to the tire with the following data fields:
* *`url`* - external link
* *`title`* - material title
* *`website`* - domain name
* *`text`* - caption text
* *`thumbnail`* - thumbnail of the external page main image (can be __*`null`*__)

**`Video`** is usually a YouTube video
* *`video_url`* - youtube link
* *`title`* - youtube title
* *`thumbnail`* - youtube thumbnail (can be __*`null`*__)

**`Benchmark`** is the tire's entry in a professional tire test or a top chart; its data structure is shown below as a response schema.

get.description:
Get list of tires matching the search query.

Search process:
* The _**`query`**_ parameter is split up by punctuation and spaces into the several chunks. 
* The chunks are matched against: `tire`, `brand`, `season`, `automobile type`, and `performance category`.
* Each matching tire gets the search score.
* The more chunks is matched by the tire, the better is the score.
* Search results are sorted by the score (relevance).

You can check out your queries at [TiresVote.com query search](https://tiresvote.com/search/).

**Note:** the API may serve only the first several result pages. The **`Paginator`** links for the remaining pages lead to _**`TiresVote.com`**_.

get.summary: Search for tires using advanced filters
get.description:
Get the list of tires matching advanced filters.

This is a simplified version of the [TiresVote.com Advanced Search](https://tiresvote.com/filter/).
Check it out for visual representation of the filters and the output list.   

All *`array`* parameters can have multiple values — repeat the parameter in the query string. For instance, `reg=north-america&reg=east-asia`. Multiple values of one parameter are combined with OR, while different parameters are combined with AND.

Parameters marked as   __*`MODES`*__   — *`tw`*, *`ar`*, *`rd`*, *`li`*, *`si`*, *`xl`*, *`ms`* — are tire modification search fields. They are applied together: a tire matches only when a single modification satisfies all of them at once. Use the *`t`* parameter to search for a specific tire modification size (for instance, `205/55R16`); it joins the same check, so the matching modification must satisfy it together with the fields above.

Two parameters are exceptions to that rule: *`nw`* carries the marker but filters tires by the model-level Nordic winter flag, and `rf=true` matches a tire when the model itself or any of its modifications is runflat.

When the *`t`* parameter is used, every returned tire carries a **`has_modes`** dictionary that maps each requested *`t`* value to the list of its matching modification sizes, or `null` when none of them match.

**Examples** — illustrative only; the sample values below are not a promise of catalog contents.

Find `michelin` summer tires having a modification in size `205/55R16` or `225/45R17` — the two *`t`* values are combined with OR, while the brand and season filters are AND-ed with them:

```http
GET https://api.wheel-size.com/v2/tires/search/advanced/?user_key=YOUR_API_KEY&b=michelin&s=summer&t=205/55R16&t=225/45R17&page=1&per_page=10
```

Response excerpt (partial — other product fields and pagination links are omitted):

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "slug": "sample-tire",
      "display": "Sample Tire",
      "brand": { "slug": "michelin", "display": "Michelin", "price_segment": "Premium" },
      "season": { "slug": "summer", "display": "Summer" },
      "has_modes": {
        "205/55R16": ["205/55 R16 91V"],
        "225/45R17": null
      }
    }
  ],
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "current_page_count": 1,
      "total_items": 1,
      "total_pages": 1
    }
  }
}
```

A tire enters **`data`** when at least one requested size matches, so its **`has_modes`** may still report `null` for the other size.

The same-modification rule illustrated — a tire matches only when a single modification has width 205, aspect ratio 55, rim diameter 16, and load index 91 all at once:

```http
GET https://api.wheel-size.com/v2/tires/search/advanced/?user_key=YOUR_API_KEY&tw=205&ar=55&rd=16&li=91
```

**Note:** the API may serve only the first several result pages. The **`Paginator`** links for the remaining pages lead to _**`TiresVote.com`**_.

get.description:
List of TiresVote.com regions.

Some tires are being sold in one geographical or economical area and aren't in another.
A TiresVote.com **`Region`** stands for an economical area of sales.
The regions division is based on manufacturers' markets and our own experience. 

Retrieve this list if you want to use a *`region`* parameter for the _**`GET /search/advanced/`**_ or _**`GET /catalog/{brand}/`**_ API methods.

List of TiresVote.com performance categories.

A **`Performance Category`** along with season and automobile type combines tires by road conditions and driving style.  
Check out [Performance Categories](https://tiresvote.com/catalog/performance/) for more information.

Retrieve this performance categories list if you want to use *`pc`* parameter for the _**`GET /search/advanced/`**_ API method.

TiresVote.com gathers **`Professional Tire Tests`** conducted by the most prominent tire-testing organizations and combines them into the tire tests catalog.

The list is paginated and can be filtered by *`year`*, *`season`* and *`automobile_type`*.

Check out [TiresVote.com Tire Tests Page](https://tiresvote.com/tests/) for more information.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description:
Benchmark release year (e.g. `2020`)
You can pass multiple values to the query string (e.g. `year=2020&year=2021`)

get.description:
Extended information about the benchmark.

A **`Benchmark`** is a **`Professional Tire Test`** or a **`Top Chart`**.

They both have identical data structure although **`Professional Tire Tests`** usually have more detailed information.
For instance, a **`Professional Tire Test`** typically provides a *`tire_size`* used in the test and a list of advantages and drawbacks for each contesting tire.  

The *`items`* list contains the participating tires ordered by their *`place`* rank, which starts at 1.

Pass one or more *`has_mode`* query parameters (tire sizes like `215/55R16`) to check size availability for every participating tire: each value maps to the list of matching size texts in *`has_modes`* of the item product, or to __*`null`*__ when no matching active size is listed for that tire.

parameters.name: slug
parameters.description: Test slug name, use _**`GET /tests/`**_ to get possible values (e.g. `2021-adac-summer-tire-test-r16`)

parameters.name: has_mode
parameters.description:
Check tire size availability for each product within the benchmark (e.g. `215/55R16`)
You can pass multiple values to the query string (e.g. `has_mode=215/55R16&has_mode=225/50R16`)
Check out *`BenchmarkItem.product.has_modes`* description inside the response schema for more information.

get.summary: Third-party tire ratings, bestsellers and top lists
get.description:
TiresVote.com gathers third-party **`Top Charts`** (**`Bestsellers`**, **`Tire Ratings`**) from the most reputable tire-selling shops and combines them into the tire top-charts catalog.

The list is paginated and can be filtered by *`year`*, *`season`* and *`automobile_type`*.

Check out [TiresVote.com Third-Party Charts Page](https://tiresvote.com/charts/) for more information.
